Chirp Analysis — one chirping oscillator, or two?

OB sniff-locked gamma (cueTask)

2026-06-30

The question

In OB sniff-locked single-trial gamma, the sniff drives a power increase whose instantaneous frequency descends (a downchirp). Is this one oscillator sweeping its frequency down, or two oscillators — a higher-frequency one earlier and a lower one later — whose sum merely looks like a chirp?

Because a single sweep and two phase-coupled overlapping tones can produce near-identical short segments, we answer the decidable form: during the transition, is there one moving spectral component or two simultaneously-present slowly-varying ones? The tests are asymmetric — each confirms one hypothesis cleanly and is mute on the other — so we read a per-session verdict vector, never a single multiplied p-value, and report “undecidable” where the evidence is mixed or the regime gives a test no teeth.

Test Positive → Engine
Phase continuity (cross-trial) single (consistent ridge-vs-Hilbert residual across trials) ridge-IF vs Hilbert phase
Envelope beating dual (beat at |f_hi−f_lo|) amplitude-envelope spectrum
Chirplet trajectory single (one descending chain) / dual (two parallel atoms) MPACT MPEM
2nd ridge / power dip leans dual FASLT + tfridge peeling
Temporal decoupling leans dual (latencies decorrelate) band-limited latencies
Spatial profile (macBP) dual (distinct hi/lo topographies) across-contact similarity

Methods (this run)

  • Scope: cueTask finals only; all macBP channels loaded, bestMac (OB) carries the core single-channel tests, the full macBP set carries the spatial test (no geometry — per design).
  • Locking: every epoch is locked to behDat.finalOnset, window [−1, +3] s (padded ±1 s for edge-free FIR/FASLT), fs = 500 Hz. No trialStart locking.
  • TF substrate: FASLT (fractional adaptive superlets), 20–70 Hz, ridge by tfridge on the 25–58 Hz power; broadband phase/envelope come from a zero-phase firws bandpass + Hilbert (never from the FASLT power).
  • Burst length (D4): per trial, the smoothed gamma-power series locked to finalOnset; burst start/stop where it rises to / falls below the 75th percentile of the cross-trial peak distribution, searched within (0, 3000] ms.
  • Synthetic Phase-0 calibration was skipped this run (it was prohibitively slow on prior attempts). Test thresholds therefore use spec defaults, and interpretation is deliberately conservative — a test “speaks” only where its mechanism has teeth in the observed cue regime (e.g. envelope beating needs ≥2 beat cycles within the coexistence window, which short cue bursts rarely afford). Decision thresholds used by the adjudicator:
test rule
phase (single) crossTrialR > 0.5 & crossTrial_p < 0.05
beat (dual) beat_fracSig >= 0.30
chirplet frac frac >= 0.40 and is the majority class
temporal corr (single) corr(latHi,latLo) >= 0.5
ridge 2nd-ridge (dual) frac trials with significant 2nd ridge >= 0.30
spatial sim ceiling mean hi/lo profile similarity < 0.5 -> dual

Conclusion

## Across 35 cue sessions: single=19, dual=0, undecidable=16.
## 
## Read per the asymmetric logic: a 'single' verdict means the SINGLE-confirming tests (phase
## cross-trial consistency, chirplet one-chain geometry) fired while the DUAL-confirming tests
## (beat, 2nd ridge, temporal/spatial decoupling) did not; 'dual' means the reverse; everything
## else is 'undecidable'. 'spatial: not assessed' (too few good contacts) is kept distinct from
## 'spatial: matched' and never averaged into the single tally.
